invariant: Identity text (comments, qualified names, path ids) uses the Java Quark local name recorded by the parser, never one re-inferred from label_to_id(label) == id. Link reversal in comments and path ids is LinkType.looksLikeRevertedForSvg after the LEFT/UP getInv, not the layout direction alone.
causal_divergence: DeploymentNode has no record of whether an alias was written, so the renderer guesses 'unaliased' whenever label_to_id(label) == id. An explicit alias that happens to equal that projection (`node "Copper Bay" as Copper_Bay`) is mistaken for an unaliased name and Rust writes 'Copper Bay' where Java writes 'Copper_Bay' (deploy_alias_collision, group_identity_collision). Separately, the no-oracle link comment prints 'reverse link' iff the direction is UP/LEFT and the path id ignores reversal of un-inverted `<--`, while Java derives both from the decorations after inversion (deploy_alias_collision: `Copper_Bay <.. Pier` is 'reverse link Copper_Bay to Pier').
planned_change: Add `quark_name: Option<String>` to DeploymentNode (serde default, omitted when None), set to the declared code when it differs from id: quoted and bracket declarations without an alias, and auto-created link endpoints. Consumers take quark_name.unwrap_or(id); qualified names keep the existing ':' segment projection. In the no-oracle edge path compute (e1, e2, decor1, decor2) from (from, to, arrow_at_end, arrow_at_start), swap for UP/LEFT, and emit the comment and path id from looksLikeRevertedForSvg / looksLikeNoDecorAtAllSvg. Class and usecase families keep their own heuristics; that stays residual under T14.23.
